clue.text: Disapprove of hiding current drop in value

indicators.note: a word hiding something holds it inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: to deprecate something is to disapprove of it
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Someone frowning on a currency quietly losing its worth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hiding' puts I (current) inside DEPRECATE, a near-twin of the answer that means something quite different.
explanation.definitionFit: Assets depreciate when their worth falls over time, a fall in value.

clue.text: Take exercise drug

parts.note: to do a drug, or do a course, is to take it
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: An instruction to work out, or an athlete taking a performance enhancer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope is slang for a narcotic, especially cannabis or performance-enhancing substances.

clue.text: Green lights for a motorway and street, northbound

parts.note: per means for each, for a, as in miles per hour
the M1 is Britain's first motorway, written here as MI

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards

explanation.surface: Traffic signals on a motorway and a street heading north.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the London to Yorkshire motorway; its 1 stands in as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Green lights in the figurative sense are approvals, which official licences grant.

clue.text: Spare millions a woman left on the side?

parts.note: a spare item is an extra one
M is short for million(s)
Rita is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A spare fortune that a woman has quietly set aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the side' is the idiom for a secret affair alongside a marriage; the question mark flags the slangy sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An affair conducted on the side is one outside wedlock, beyond the marriage.

clue.text: Press caught boy in battleship

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A press-ganged boy captured and put aboard a warship.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironclads were armoured steam warships of the nineteenth century, early battle vessels.

clue.text: What a person carries spills

indicators.note: the phrase what a person carries holds the letters inside it, within its words

explanation.surface: A question about what someone is carrying when they spill something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spills' looks like a verb; it is a noun, thin strips of wood or paper used to light fires.
explanation.definitionFit: Spills and tapers are both slender wicks or slips used to carry a flame to a fire or candle.

clue.text: Push five to leave Oxford?

indicators.note: letters told to leave a word are taken out of it

parts.note: to shove is to push
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Someone shoving a group of five students out of Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: An Oxford is a laced leather shoe; the question mark marks the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oxford is a classic style of laced footwear, an example of the item.

clue.text: Dress at home

parts.note: a habit is a monk's or nun's dress, or a riding dress

explanation.surface: Getting dressed while at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural habitat is the place where an animal or plant lives, its home.

clue.text: Initiative to go into force

parts.note: to enter is to go into
to prise something open is to force it

explanation.surface: Taking the initiative to break into somewhere by force.
explanation.definitionFit: Enterprise means resourcefulness and readiness to undertake new projects, initiative.

clue.text: Trail volunteers returning in pursuit of normal soldiers

indicators.note: coming in pursuit of something means following it, so this piece comes after

parts.note: par is the normal or standard level

indicators.note: returning signals the trail and volunteers read backwards

parts.note: spoor is the track or trail of an animal
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: Volunteers retracing a trail behind regular soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's part-time volunteer reserve; 'returning' reverses the trail and volunteers together.
explanation.definitionFit: Paratroops are airborne troops dropped by parachute, a kind of soldier.

clue.text: Just over half of Beatles worked to make 'Help!'

indicators.note: letters that are worked are reshaped into a new order
just over half of a seven-letter word is its first four letters

explanation.surface: How the Beatles produced their song Help!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just over half of' takes BEAT from Beatles; 'worked' rearranges BEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to help or assist, usually in wrongdoing; here the song title is the verb.

clue.text: Republican in terribly close battle for election

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other, placed inside it
terribly suggests the words are badly mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A Republican caught up in a terribly close election battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges CLOSE BATTLE into SECETBALLOT, and 'in' places R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret ballot is the method of election in which votes are cast privately.

clue.text: Sleazy club putting out energy for a prima donna

indicators.note: putting out one letter and setting another in its place swaps them

parts.note: a dive is a sleazy bar or club
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A seedy nightclub turning away a star singer.
explanation.definitionFit: A diva is a celebrated female opera singer, the leading lady of a company.

clue.text: Go in after fish and chips

indicators.note: one piece placed after another follows it

parts.note: a carp is a freshwater fish
to enter is to go in

explanation.surface: An invitation to go and eat fish and chips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chips' is the old nickname for a ship's woodworker, and a chippy is British slang for a woodworker.
explanation.definitionFit: Chips was the traditional naval nickname for the ship's woodworker, one who chips wood.

clue.text: Finally be amusing about working and saving money

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word be
one word placed about another goes around it

parts.note: comical means amusing
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A plea to be funny about one's job while thrifty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' takes only the last letter of 'be'; 'about' wraps the amusing word around the working one.
explanation.definitionFit: Being economical means thrifty, careful to avoid waste and spend little.

clue.text: One's alone with actors not present

parts.note: the cast is the set of actors in a production
someone away is not present

explanation.surface: A lonely performer left by the rest of the company.
explanation.definitionFit: A castaway is a shipwrecked person stranded by himself on a remote island.

clue.text: Hole found in old vehicle beginning to rust

parts.note: a crate is slang for an old, ramshackle car

indicators.note: beginning to a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A hole discovered in an old banger as it starts to rust.
explanation.definitionFit: A crater is a bowl-shaped hollow in the ground, a hole.

clue.text: Elements of football and cricket used in religious festival

parts.note: a pass is one element of play in football
an over is a set of six balls bowled in cricket

explanation.surface: Sporting elements borrowed for a religious celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Passover is the Jewish spring feast commemorating the Exodus from Egypt.

clue.text: Fool can upset with humour

indicators.note: in an across clue upset turns the word can over, reading it backwards

parts.note: a tin is a can
wit is humour

explanation.surface: A clown who can upset people with his jokes.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitwit is a silly or stupid person, an idiot.

clue.text: Non-drinker imbibing an alcoholic drink in temper

indicators.note: imbibing means taking in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: TT means teetotal, a non-drinker
rum is an alcoholic spirit

explanation.surface: A teetotaller drinking spirits and flying into a rage.
explanation.definitionFit: A tantrum is an outburst of bad temper, a fit of rage.

clue.text: 18 goes over and samples baked goods

indicators.note: going over means turning back, so the word reads in reverse

parts.note: 18 across is a fool, and a sap is a fool
to sample is to try, so samples gives tries

explanation.surface: A fool goes back for seconds of the cakes.
explanation.walkthrough: '18' points to the answer of 18 across, for which SAP is another word.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastries are small baked confections made of dough or pastry.

clue.text: Tooth made from zinc is 'orrible

indicators.note: the letters are made from a run across these words

explanation.surface: A Cockney complaining that a metal false tooth is horrible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orrible is horrible with the h dropped, Cockney style.
explanation.definitionFit: An incisor is one of the narrow-edged front teeth used for cutting.

clue.text: Engineers sit and rest

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers of the British Army
to sit for a portrait is to pose

explanation.surface: Engineers taking a seat for a breather.
explanation.definitionFit: Repose is a state of rest, sleep or tranquillity.

clue.text: Shock at zebras regularly becoming dangerous animals

parts.note: a shock of hair is a mane

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of the word zebras

explanation.surface: Zebras getting a fright and turning nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Lions and tigers that hunt people are man-eaters, perilous beasts.

clue.text: Main bridge?

definitions.meaning: chief or principal, as in a leading enemy
a curved span supporting a bridge, or the bridge itself

explanation.definitionFit: As a prefix or adjective it means principal; as a structure it is a curved span.

clue.text: Auntie's complaint cut short bishop

indicators.note: a word cut short loses its final letter

parts.note: a beef is a grumble or complaint
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: An aunt's grievance about a bishop being curtailed.
explanation.walkthrough: Auntie and the Beeb are both British nicknames for the BBC, the public broadcaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are affectionate nicknames for the British Broadcasting Corporation.

clue.text: Short dog with tail? Just its tip

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

indicators.note: only the tip, the first letter, of the word tail is taken

explanation.surface: A little dog with a stub of a tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A curt reply is brief to the point of rudeness, short.

clue.text: Cold? Once salve works, recover

parts.note: C stands for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: works suggests the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A cold sufferer getting better once the ointment takes effect.
explanation.definitionFit: To convalesce is to regain health and strength after illness.

clue.text: I am cutting weight in half to become member

indicators.note: cutting a word in half means sitting inside it

parts.note: LB is the abbreviation for a pound weight
I'm is a contraction of I am

explanation.surface: Someone slimming to get into a club.
explanation.definitionFit: A limb is an arm or leg, a bodily member.

clue.text: Both rather fancy dish

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective suggests the letters are elaborately reworked

explanation.surface: Two people both quite keen on a particular meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dish' is slang for an attractive person, not food.
explanation.definitionFit: A good-looking person is called a dish, and a heartthrob is one adored for looks.
